mainTopic: Shabbat 90a: minimum amounts (שיעורים) for carrying out spices, dyes, laundry materials, and כל שהוא items on שבת
overview: This amud finishes the list of minimum amounts (שיעורים) for carrying things out on שבת. First the גמרא explains that different spices join together only when they can sweeten one pot. It then resolves a contradiction about dye-materials: dry materials need enough to dye a small garment, but herbs that are already soaked count at a tiny sample. Next it identifies the laundry materials of the משנה. After three tries, בורית turns out to be one kind of aloe. A new משנה rules that pepper, tar, perfumes, metals, holy items stored for גניזה, and, according to רבי יהודה, items of עבודה זרה count at כל שהוא. The גמרא gives the use of each tiny amount, and it adds a side discussion about the minimum for vows to donate iron and copper to the בית המקדש. It warns that insects in fruit are dangerous, with a story from the time of רבי יוחנן. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a peddler's basket brings only one חטאת, and it gives the amount for garden seeds.

steps.title: Spice types combine only when they are sweetening spices
steps.stepSummary: An earlier-quoted statement limits the rule that different spices join together: it applies only to sweetening spices, because they can all sweeten one pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: They taught this rule only about sweet types of spices, because they are fit to sweeten a pot together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement, quoted in the discussion on the previous amud, saying that different kinds of spices join together only when they are sweet spices. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that different spices can count together toward one minimum amount only if they do the same job. Sweet spices all sweeten a dish, so together they form one useful amount. This raises a problem for our משנה, which says spices combine without any such limit.

keyTerms.meaning: a cooking pot (the dish in it)
they join together to make the minimum amount (the topic under discussion)

phrases.english: They taught this about sweet types,
phrases.notes: This narrows an earlier teaching that said different spices combine together.

phrases.english: since they are fit to sweeten a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier סוגיא about spices combining.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different kinds of spices combine for a minimum amount only when they are sweeteners that can work together in one pot.

steps.title: Inference: spices that cannot sweeten together do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the statement carefully: if only sweet spices combine, then other spices should not, which seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason they combine is that they can sweeten the pot. But if that is not so, they do not combine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the statement and uses it to challenge our משנה, which said spices combine with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'because they can sweeten' imply that without this feature there is no combining. Our משנה says plainly 'and they combine with one another', with no condition. So the inference seems to contradict the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: but if not so, then not (an inference from the reason)

phrases.english: The reason is that they are fit to sweeten the pot,
but if that is not so, they do not combine!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דַּחֲזוּ לְמַתֵּק אֶת הַקְּדֵירָה, הָא לָאו הָכִי — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from step 1 and turns it against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's unqualified statement that spices combine with one another.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If combining depends on being able to sweeten together, spices that cannot do so should not combine. Yet the משנה states combining without any condition.

steps.title: Our משנה also speaks of spices that can sweeten together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה also refers to spices fit to sweeten a pot, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the משנה is talking about spices that are fit to sweeten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by reading our משנה as dealing with the same kind of spices, ones that sweeten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is retracted. The condition 'they can sweeten together' is simply read into our משנה as well. Both sources now agree: spices combine when they serve one purpose in the dish.
steps.whatToRemember: Different spices count together toward the minimum amount only when they work together for the same purpose, like sweetening one pot.

phrases.english: Here too, they are fit to sweeten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to say all spices combine, with no condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה refers to sweetening spices, matching the condition.

steps.title: משנה quote: the amount of dye-materials is enough to dye a small garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: nutshells, pomegranate peels, safflower and madder, all used for dyeing, have a minimum amount of enough to dye a small garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nutshells, pomegranate peels, safflower and madder: the amount is enough to dye a small garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה about dye-materials. It is setting up a contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These materials are used to make dyes. The משנה says one is liable for carrying them out on שבת only if he carries enough to dye a small garment, such as the small cloth on top of a woman's hairnet.

keyTerms.meaning: safflower (or woad) and madder, plants used for dye

phrases.english: enough to dye a small garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum amount for carrying out dye-materials is enough to dye a small garment.

steps.title: Contradiction: soaked dye-herbs need only enough for a tiny sample
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says that for soaked dye-herbs the amount is only enough to dye a tiny wool sample for the loom's shuttle, which is smaller than a small garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a contradiction was raised: One who carries out soaked herbs is liable for enough to dye with them a sample for the shuttle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one משנה against another: one says 'a small garment', the other says 'a tiny sample'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources deal with dyeing materials, but they give different minimum amounts. A sample for the loom is much smaller than a small garment. So which amount is correct?

keyTerms.meaning: and a contradiction was raised from another source

phrases.english: And a contradiction was raised: One who carries out soaked herbs —
enough to dye with them a sample for the shuttle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the amount given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's amount of 'enough to dye a small garment'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה gives a much smaller amount, a tiny sample, for dye-materials.

steps.title: Soaked herbs are already prepared, so a smaller amount counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב נחמן's quote of רבה בר אבוה: no one soaks herbs just to dye a tiny sample, so herbs that are already soaked count even at a small amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about that: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה, because a person does not bother to soak herbs to dye a sample for the shuttle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the contradiction was already resolved: soaked herbs and dry herbs are different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dry dye-materials matter only in an amount worth soaking, and people soak only for a real garment. Once herbs are already soaked and ready, even a tiny amount is useful for a sample, so it counts. Each משנה speaks of a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: wasn't it already stated about it
an Amora who reports the answer
רב נחמן's teacher, the source of the answer

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the answer as 'soaked herbs need a bigger amount'. It is the reverse: people only start soaking for a real garment, so dry herbs need a garment's worth. Herbs already soaked count even at the tiny sample amount.

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated about it:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
because a person does not bother
to dye with them a sample for the shuttle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (dry vs. already-soaked herbs)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to set one amount for the same dye-materials.
steps.terutzMaskana: Unsoaked materials need a garment's worth. Already-soaked herbs need only a sample's worth.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic rule of שבת amounts: what counts as significant depends on how people really use the item in its current state.

steps.title: Urine for laundering is up to forty days old
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the urine in the משנה, used for cleaning clothes, means urine up to forty days old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Urine: it was taught, urine up to forty days old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the laundry materials in the משנה, starting with urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Urine was used as a cleaning agent. After forty days it loses its strength and is no longer useful for washing, so it is not what the משנה means.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: מֵי רַגְלַיִם עַד בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: It was taught: urine up to forty days old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה (laundry materials).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urine counts as a laundry agent only up to forty days old.

steps.title: The natron meant is Alexandrian natron
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the natron in the משנה is Alexandrian natron, not natron from Anpantrin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Natron: it was taught, Alexandrian natron, and not Anpantrin natron.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next laundry material, natron, by saying which kind is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were different kinds of natron (a soda-like cleaning mineral) of different quality. The משנה's amount refers to the Alexandrian kind.

keyTerms.meaning: natron, a mineral used for washing
Anpantrin, a place whose natron is a different kind

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the list of laundry materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The natron in the משנה is Alexandrian natron.

steps.title: רב יהודה: בורית is sand
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה identifies the בורית of the משנה as sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: בורית: רב יהודה said, this is sand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב יהודה's first identification of בורית, which will soon be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בורית is an unclear word. רב יהודה suggests it is a kind of sand used to scrub clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: a cleaning substance named in the משנה; its identity is debated

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is sand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next laundry material.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists בורית and sand separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists 'בורית and sand' as two items, so בורית cannot be sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: the בורית and the sand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a ברייתא that names both items side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two things appear separately in one list, they must be different things. So בורית cannot simply mean sand.

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: the borit and the sand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בורית is sand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists בורית and sand as two separate items, so they cannot be the same thing.

steps.title: Second proposal: בורית is sulphur
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops 'sand' and suggests that בורית is sulphur.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is בורית? Sulphur.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'sand' failed, the גמרא offers a new meaning for בורית: sulphur.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means the earlier answer is dropped. Sulphur fits the ברייתא, which lists בורית separately from sand. This new suggestion will be tested next.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected identification of step 9.

steps.title: בורית is under שביעית laws, but sulphur would not be
steps.stepSummary: A source says the Sages added בורית to the list of things subject to שביעית. Sulphur, a mineral, cannot be subject to שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: They added to them bulbs of ornithogalum, wormwood, בורית, and aloe. And if you think it is sulphur, is sulphur subject to שביעית?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to 'sulphur' from a source that lists בורית among growing plants covered by שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שביעית laws apply to things that grow from the land. The source places בורית among plants such as aloe. Sulphur is a mineral that does not grow, so it should not appear in such a list.

keyTerms.meaning: they added to them (to the list)
the Sabbatical year and its laws for produce
and if it would enter your mind

phrases.english: They objected: They added to them
And if it enters your mind that it is sulphur,
is sulphur subject to the Sabbatical year?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new identification of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בורית is sulphur.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בורית is listed as subject to שביעית, which applies only to growing things. Sulphur does not grow.

steps.title: Proof: only rooted, growing things have שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its objection with a משנה: anything with a root has שביעית, and anything without a root does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And didn't we learn: This is the rule: anything that has a root is subject to שביעית, and anything without a root is not subject to שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the challenge of the previous step with a clear rule from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule proves that minerals like sulphur, which have no root, are outside שביעית. So the source listing בורית as subject to שביעית cannot mean sulphur.

keyTerms.meaning: and didn't we learn in a משנה

phrases.english: And didn't we learn: This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עִיקָּר — יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: anything that has a root is subject to the Sabbatical year,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ עִיקָּר — אֵין לוֹ שְׁבִיעִית!
phrases.english: and anything without a root is not subject to the Sabbatical year!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the objection in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That sulphur cannot be subject to שביעית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule: only things with a root are subject to שביעית.

steps.title: Third proposal: בורית is aloe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops 'sulphur' and suggests that בורית is aloe, a growing plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is בורית? Aloe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third meaning, aloe, which grows and so fits the שביעית list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aloe has a root, so it can be subject to שביעית. This avoids the problem with sulphur, but it will face its own challenge.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected identification of step 11.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists בורית and aloe separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא names 'בורית and aloe' as two items, so בורית cannot simply be aloe.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: בורית and aloe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the aloe answer the same way it challenged 'sand': the two are listed separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reasoning applies again: two items in one list must be different. Indeed, the שביעית list just quoted also says 'and בורית and aloe'.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: borit and aloe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בורית is aloe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בורית and aloe are listed as two separate items, so they cannot be identical.

steps.title: Conclusion: there are two kinds of aloe, and בורית is one of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that there are two kinds of aloe. One is called בורית, which explains why the lists name them separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there are two kinds of aloe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question: בורית is a kind of aloe, distinct from the other kind simply called 'aloe'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer satisfies every source. As a plant with a root, בורית fits the שביעית list, and as a separate kind of aloe it can be listed next to 'aloe'. The identification is refined rather than dropped.
steps.whatToRemember: בורית went through three proposals. Sand was rejected because it is listed separately. Sulphur was rejected because it has no root and so has no שביעית. The final answer is that בורית is one of two kinds of aloe.

phrases.english: Rather, there are two kinds of aloe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 15 and closes the בורית discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בורית is one of two varieties of aloe. This fits both its listing beside aloe and its being subject to שביעית.

steps.title: רב יהודה identifies קימוליא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that קימוליא, a cleaning agent from the previous משנה, is the earth called 'שלוף דוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the קימוליא in the משנה, רב יהודה said: it is the earth called 'pull out, stick in' (שלוף דוץ).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining the unfamiliar cleaning materials from the previous משנה. Now it identifies קימוליא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a definition, not an argument. רב יהודה gives the everyday name people used for this cleaning clay so we know what material the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Cimolian earth, a clay used for washing
'Pull out, stick in', the popular name of this clay

phrases.notes: A nickname for this type of clay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling what בורית is, the גמרא moves on to the next cleaning agent in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קימוליא is the earth known as שלוף דוץ.

steps.title: שמואל identifies אשלג from sailors' report
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asked seafarers about אשלג. They told him it is called שונאגא, it is found in pearl shells, and it is taken out with an iron skewer.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the אשלג, שמואל said: I asked all the sailors, and they told me it is called 'שונאגא'. It is found in the hollow of the pearl shell, and they take it out with an iron skewer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the last cleaning agent, אשלג. שמואל relies on what sailors told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אשלג was not a local material, so שמואל went to the experts who knew the sea. This finishes the list of cleaning agents from the previous משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaning substance from the sea

phrases.english: and they told me its name is 'shunaga',
and it is found in the hollow of the pearl shell,
and they take it out with an iron skewer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁלָג, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שְׁאֵילְתִּינְהוּ לְכֹל נָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues identifying the cleaning agents. This one is the last item on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשלג is the substance sailors call שונאגא. It is found in pearl shells.
steps.whatToRemember: The cleaning agents from the previous משנה are now all identified: בורית (a kind of aloe), קימוליא (a clay), and אשלג (a substance from pearl shells).

steps.title: New משנה: pepper, tar, perfumes and metals at any amount
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that carrying out even the smallest amount of pepper, tar, perfumes, or metals on שבת makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Pepper: any amount. Tar: any amount. Kinds of perfumes and kinds of metals: any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items where carrying out even a tiny bit on שבת is enough to be חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a minimum שיעור before carrying is a punishable מלאכה. For these items, even a tiny amount is useful or valued, so the שיעור is כל שהוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest

steps.confusionAlert: כל שהוא does not mean these items have no measure at all. It means the measure for being חייב is the smallest amount. The item is still part of the regular category of הוצאה.

phrases.aramaic: מִינֵי בְשָׂמִים וּמִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת — כׇּל שֶׁהֵן.
phrases.english: Kinds of perfumes and kinds of metals: any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It continues the chapter's theme of carrying measures, now for items with the smallest measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pepper, tar, perfumes, and metals: one is חייב for carrying out any amount.

steps.title: Holy items stored for burial at any amount
steps.stepSummary: Stones and earth of the מזבח, and holy scrolls or covers worn out by insects, have a שיעור of כל שהוא, because people store them away for burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the stones of the מזבח or the earth of the מזבח, or from scrolls eaten by insects or their insect-eaten covers: any amount. This is because people put them away in order to bury them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second group of items, holy objects. It gives the reason why even a tiny piece counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These items are not useful in a practical way. They count because people treat even a small piece as important and save it for גניזה. Since people guard even a crumb, carrying a crumb is a real act of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Insect-eaten remains, or the insect that eats books
To bury them, out of respect (גניזה)

phrases.english: From the stones of the altar or the earth of the altar,
insect-eaten scrolls and insect-eaten scroll covers:
because people store them away in order to bury them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second group of כל שהוא items. These count for a different reason: holiness, not usefulness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy items that are stored for גניזה have a שיעור of כל שהוא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a שיעור can come from how people value an item, not only from what it can be used for.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds items of idolatry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that even carrying out items used for עבודה זרה makes one חייב at any amount. His source is the פסוק 'Let nothing of the חרם cling to your hand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even one who carries out items used for עבודה זרה is חייב for any amount. As the פסוק says: 'And nothing of the banned items shall cling to your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds one more item to the list, objects of עבודה זרה. He brings a פסוק to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah wants even the smallest piece of עבודה זרה destroyed. So a person takes even a tiny bit seriously, carrying it out in order to get rid of it. That gives it a שיעור of כל שהוא.

keyTerms.meaning: Banned or forbidden items that must be destroyed
Anything at all, even the slightest

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמּוֹצִיא מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — כׇּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.english: Even one who carries out accessories of idolatry: any amount,
'And nothing of the banned items shall cling to your hand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמּוֹצִיא מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more item to the list. It is based on the importance of destroying עבודה זרה rather than holiness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, items of עבודה זרה have a שיעור of כל שהוא.

steps.title: What use is a tiny bit of pepper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what possible use a tiny amount of pepper has, since that is why it would count.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Pepper at any amount: what is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It asks what a crumb of pepper could be used for. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying only counts if the amount is useful. So the גמרא needs to find a use for even a tiny bit of pepper to explain the משנה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for? What use does it have?

phrases.english: Pepper, any amount: for what is it fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the first item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What use a tiny amount of pepper has.

steps.title: Pepper is for bad breath
steps.stepSummary: Even a tiny bit of pepper is useful for fixing bad breath.
steps.simpleTranslation: For bad breath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a little pepper is used to freshen the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one peppercorn helps with mouth odor. So a tiny amount has a real use, and carrying it counts.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about pepper.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tiny amount of pepper is useful against bad breath.

steps.title: What use is a tiny bit of tar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about tar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tar at any amount: what is it good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what use a tiny bit of tar has. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same logic as with pepper. To count as carrying, even a tiny amount must have a real use.

phrases.english: Tar, any amount: for what is it fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second item in the משנה, using the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What use a tiny amount of tar has.

steps.title: Tar is for headaches
steps.stepSummary: Even a tiny bit of tar is useful as a remedy for headaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a headache.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a little tar was used to treat headaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small dab of tar was a known headache remedy. So a tiny amount is useful, and carrying it counts.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about tar.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tiny amount of tar is useful for headaches.

steps.title: ברייתא adds bad smells, fine oil, purple dye and rosebuds
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's perfumes, a ברייתא adds that a foul-smelling substance, fine oil, and purple dye are all כל שהוא. A young rosebud counts at one bud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Kinds of perfumes: any amount.' The רבנן taught: One who carries out something with a bad smell: any amount. Fine oil: any amount. Purple dye: any amount. A young rosebud: one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about perfumes. Then it brings a ברייתא that adds more items with the same tiny שיעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smell-related items are useful even in tiny amounts. The ברייתא adds that this is true even for a bad smell, which can be used as a remedy. A rosebud is set at one whole bud, since that is the smallest useful unit.

phrases.english: One who carries out a foul odor: any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִינֵי בְּשָׂמִים — כׇּל שֶׁהֵן. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the perfume item in the משנה. It expands that item using a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A foul odor, fine oil, and purple dye are כל שהוא. A young rosebud counts at one bud.

steps.title: What use is a tiny bit of metal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about metals and asks what a tiny piece of metal is good for.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Kinds of metals: any amount.' What are they good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the metals in the משנה. It asks what use a tiny bit could have, which sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crumb of metal seems useless. So the גמרא needs a practical use to justify the כל שהוא ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they fit for? (plural form)

steps.triggerLanguage: מִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת — כׇּל שֶׁהֵן. לְמַאי חֲזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the metals item. It asks the same 'what use' question as with pepper and tar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What use a tiny amount of metal has.

steps.title: Metal can make a small goad
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that even a small bit of metal can be made into a small goad, so it is useful.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Because it is fit to make a small goad from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Even a little metal can be shaped into a small pointed tool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small point or goad needs only a tiny bit of metal. That makes even a small amount useful, which explains the כל שהוא ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A goad, a pointed tip for prodding animals

steps.whatToRemember: Every כל שהוא item in this משנה has a reason. Practical items like pepper, tar, perfumes, and metal are useful even in tiny amounts. Holy items and items of עבודה זרה are treated as important even in tiny amounts.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Because it is fit to make from it

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: שֶׁכֵּן רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנָּה דׇּרְבָן קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about metals.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tiny amount of metal is useful because it can be made into a small goad.

steps.title: A vow to donate iron must be at least a cubit by a cubit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if someone vows to give iron to the הקדש without naming an amount, אחרים say he must give at least a piece one אמה by one אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone says, "I take upon myself to give iron," אחרים say he may not give less than a cubit by a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a vow to donate iron to the בית המקדש. It comes up here because the גמרא was just talking about small pieces of metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not say how much iron he would give. The ברייתא sets a minimum amount that counts as keeping his vow. That minimum is a piece one אמה by one אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me": the words a person uses to make a vow to donate
"Others": a name for a תנא (traditionally רבי מאיר)
A cubit by a cubit (a square about 1.5–2 feet on each side)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a side topic. It is about vows to the הקדש, not about carrying on שבת. The גמרא brings it only because both topics deal with minimum amounts of metal.

phrases.english: One who says, "It is upon me to give iron,"
He may not give less than a cubit by a cubit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the minimum amount of metal for carrying on שבת to a related topic: the minimum amount of metal for a vow to the הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified vow of iron requires at least one אמה by one אמה.

steps.title: What is that size of iron used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what use the בית המקדש has for a piece of iron that size.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this exact size was chosen. What would the בית המקדש do with it? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minimum amount usually matches some real use. The גמרא wants to know which use in the בית המקדש fits a piece one אמה by one אמה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for? What is it used for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the measurement given in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What use in the בית המקדש fits a piece of iron one אמה by one אמה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: It is used for the anti-raven cover
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that this size of iron was used for the כלייא עורב, the iron cover on the roof of the בית המקדש that kept ravens away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: For a raven-preventer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. A piece of iron this size can be used as part of the cover that kept ravens off the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roof of the בית המקדש was covered with iron sheets that had sharp points sticking up, so birds could not land there. A sheet one אמה by one אמה is one usable section of that cover. So the minimum amount matches a real need in the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A "raven-preventer": spiked iron plates on the roof of the בית המקדש that stopped ravens from landing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The iron is used for the כלייא עורב on the roof.

steps.title: Another version: the minimum is whatever a raven-preventer needs
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the ברייתא has אחרים setting the minimum as the amount needed for a כלייא עורב, instead of naming a size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: אחרים say he may not give less than a raven-preventer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same teaching. In this version, אחרים name the use (a raven-preventer) and not the size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions end up in the same place. The only difference is which part is in the ברייתא and which part רב יוסף supplies. In the first version the ברייתא gives the size and רב יוסף explains the use. In this version the ברייתא gives the use, and the size will be explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a different version of a teaching

phrases.english: He may not give less than a raven-preventer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the ברייתא from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum for a vow of iron is the amount needed for a כלייא עורב.

steps.title: How much iron is a raven-preventer?
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the גמרא asks how big a raven-preventer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is that?
steps.whatsHappening: Since this version did not give a size, the גמרא asks what the size is. This question sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minimum like "enough for a raven-preventer" is not clear enough to follow in practice. The גמרא needs an actual measurement.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact size meant in the second version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of a כלייא עורב.

steps.title: רב יוסף: A cubit by a cubit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that a raven-preventer is one אמה by one אמה, so both versions give the same amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A cubit by a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the size: one אמה by one אמה. This is the same amount as in the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב יוסף supplies the size instead of the use. Either way, the practical law is the same: give a piece of iron one אמה by one אמה.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow of iron with no amount named requires one אמה by one אמה, which is the size of a section of the anti-raven cover on the roof of the בית המקדש.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 and shows both versions agree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כלייא עורב is one אמה by one אמה.

steps.title: A vow of copper must be worth at least a silver מעה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: someone who vows copper must give at least the value of a silver מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Copper: he may not give less than a silver מעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from iron to copper. It sets the minimum for a vow of copper by its value: at least one silver מעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For iron, the minimum was a size. For copper, the minimum is a money value. Copper worth one מעה is the least amount that counts as keeping the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver ma'ah, a small coin
He may not give less than

phrases.english: Copper: he may not give less than the value of a silver ma'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא, moving from iron to copper.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified vow of copper requires copper worth at least one silver מעה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: At least enough for a small copper hook
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר, who says the minimum for copper is the amount needed for a small copper hook.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, he may not give less than a small copper hook.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion. רבי אליעזר measures the minimum for copper by a useful tool, a small hook, and not by money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion measured copper by its value. רבי אליעזר measures it by what can actually be made from it, the same way iron was measured by the raven-preventer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A small hook or pointed tool

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִצִּינּוֹרָא קְטַנָּה שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת.
phrases.english: He may not give less than a small copper hook.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion about the minimum for copper.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified vow of copper requires enough copper to make a small hook.

steps.title: What is a small copper hook used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the בית המקדש uses a small copper hook for.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what job this small hook does in the בית המקדש. This question sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the iron, the minimum has to match a real use in the בית המקדש. The גמרא wants to know that use.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the use of the hook from step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a small copper hook is used for in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: אביי: It cleans the wicks and lamps of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the hook is used to clear out the wicks and clean the lamps of the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They use it to scrape out the wicks and clean the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers. The small hook is used to take care of the מנורה: scraping out old wicks and cleaning the lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cleaning the lamps of the מנורה was a daily job, so a small hook had a real use in the בית המקדש. That is why רבי אליעזר used it as the minimum for copper.
steps.whatToRemember: Vow minimums are tied to real uses in the בית המקדש: iron for the raven-preventer, copper for the hook that cleans the מנורה (according to רבי אליעזר).

phrases.english: That they scrape out the wicks with it

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁמְּחַטְּטִין בָּהּ אֶת הַפְּתִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 and closes the side topic of vows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hook is used to scrape out wicks and clean the lamps of the מנורה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Insects that eat books, silk, and fruit are dangerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about מקק. רבי יהודה then lists insects that eat books, silk, grapes, figs, and pomegranates, and says all of them are dangerous to swallow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: book-insects and cloth-insects. רבי יהודה said: The book-insect, the silk-insect, the grape-insect, the fig-insect, and the pomegranate-insect are all dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its words about insects that eat scrolls and their covers. רבי יהודה adds a list of similar insects and warns that every one of them is dangerous to swallow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned מקק only to explain why worn-out scrolls and covers are still carried. רבי יהודה uses the word to teach a health warning. Each type of food or material has its own insect, and swallowing any of them is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: An insect that eats books or cloth
Insects found in grapes, figs, and pomegranates

phrases.english: The mekak of books, the tekhakh of silk,
and the ayla of grapes, and the pah of figs,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקַק סְפָרִים וּמְקַק מִטְפָּחֹת. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of vows and returns to explaining the words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Insects found in books, silk, grapes, figs, and pomegranates are all dangerous to swallow.

steps.title: A student dies from the fig insect
steps.stepSummary: A student eating figs in front of רבי יוחנן asked whether figs have thorns. רבי יוחנן answered that the fig insect had killed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A student was sitting before רבי יוחנן, eating figs. He said, "רבי, are there thorns in figs?" רבי יוחנן said, "The פה (fig insect) has killed this one."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows how real the danger is. The student felt something sharp in his throat. רבי יוחנן understood that the fig insect had pricked him and that it would kill him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Figs have no thorns, so the sharp feeling had to come from the insect inside. The story backs up רבי יהודה's warning that the פה of figs is deadly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רבי יהודה's warning from a general statement into a real case, which shows why one must check fruit carefully before eating.

phrases.english: who was sitting before Rabbi Yochanan
He said to him: My teacher,
The pah (fig insect) has killed this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תַּלְמִידָא דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows with a real event that רבי יהודה's warning is true.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's claim that the פה of figs is dangerous.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the student who died after eating figs in front of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: New משנה: A peddler's basket is only one sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that carrying out a peddler's basket with many kinds of items in it brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who carries out a peddler's basket, even though it has many kinds of items in it, is only obligated to bring one sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that one act of carrying brings only one חטאת, even if the basket holds many different items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think each type of item counts as a separate sin. The משנה says the count follows the number of acts, not the number of items. Taking out one basket is one act of הוצאה, so there is one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
A peddler's basket (holding spices, perfumes, jewelry)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule for counting חטאות on שבת: what matters is the number of acts, not the number of objects.

phrases.english: One who carries out a peddler's basket,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מִינִין הַרְבֵּה —
phrases.english: even though there are many types in it —
is only obligated to bring one sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One act of carrying out a basket of many types of items brings only one חטאת.

steps.title: Garden seeds: less than a dried fig, or five seeds
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the amount for carrying garden seeds is less than a גרוגרת. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says it is five seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Garden seeds: less than a dried fig. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: five.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the minimum amount of garden seeds that makes a person liable for carrying them on שבת. The first opinion says less than a גרוגרת. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says the amount is five seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food is usually measured by a גרוגרת. Seeds meant for planting get a smaller amount, because even a few seeds are useful for planting. רבי יהודה בן בתירה makes this into a count of five seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a dried fig, the usual amount for food on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: "Less than a גרוגרת" here means the amount for liability is smaller than the usual food amount. It does not mean that carrying less than a גרוגרת is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר: חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: Five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the new משנה with a second law about minimum amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount for carrying garden seeds is less than a גרוגרת. According to רבי יהודה בן בתירה it is five seeds.
